*   **Residual Stream Dimension (d_{\text{model}}):** The residual dimension \(d_{\text{model}}\) is a crucial parameter in transformer models. It represents the number of parameters that are "frozen" during the forward pass.  A larger residual dimension allows the model to learn more complex representations, but it also increases the computational cost of the forward pass.

*   **Attention Head Dimension (d_{\text{attn}}):** The attention head dimension \(d_{\text{attn}}\) is a key factor in the model's ability to focus on relevant parts of the input sequence.  A larger attention head allows the model to capture more complex relationships between words, leading to better performance on tasks requiring long-range dependencies.

*   **Feedforward Network Dimension (d_{\text{ff}}):** The feedforward network dimension \(d_{\text{ff}}\) is a measure of the model's capacity to process the entire input sequence. A larger dimension means the model can handle more information and can learn more complex representations.

*   **Intermediate Feedforward Network Dimension (d_{\text{ff}}):** The intermediate feedforward network dimension \(d_{\text{ff}}\) is a measure of the model's capacity to process the intermediate representations of the input sequence. A larger dimension means the model can handle more intermediate representations.
